content.text: The text chiefly recounts General Charles Gordon’s mission to Sudan in 1884. Britain sent him to Khartoum to evacuate Egyptian garrisons, despite his belief that the Mahdi’s power had to be defeated. Delays, governmental indecision, and opposition to Zebehr weakened his position. Gordon travelled from Cairo to Khartoum, organized its defenses, and held the city under siege while requesting reinforcements. A delayed British relief expedition reached the Nile too late; Khartoum fell on January 26, 1885, and Gordon was killed. The narrative blames Lord Cromer for delaying Gordon’s appointment and Lord Wolseley for the failed rescue. Later excerpts describe fictional expeditions in Africa, the recovery of Anderson Rover, and religious persecution under the Inquisition.
